idiom_name: MockK strict mock of the service interface (coEvery for suspend operations)
implementation_notes: MockK is written for Kotlin: mockk<PriceService>() stands in for an interface or class, every { } returns and coEvery for suspend functions declare canned behaviour, the default behaviour is strict so an unexpected call fails the test, and object mocks cover production code that has no interface at all. For a Ktor client the cheaper seam is the engine: MockEngine answers from a handler lambda and is injected into HttpClient, so the real client pipeline, content negotiation and status handling run against canned responses. A plain fake class implementing the interface remains the best option when the stand-in needs behaviour instead of recorded interactions.
pitfalls: MockK instruments classes through a Java agent: on JDK 21 and later the runtime prints a dynamic-agent warning unless the agent is loaded explicitly, and spies or static mocks can hit InaccessibleObjectException on JDK 16 and above.
Inline functions cannot be mocked at all, and relaxed mocks answer every call with a default, which hides missing stubs - keep the strict default.
Suspend functions need coEvery and coVerify; the blocking variants never match and the failure message points at the matcher rather than at the missing co-prefix.

variants.name: Ktor MockEngine under the real HttpClient
variants.implementation_notes: Ktor ships a mock engine that simulates HTTP calls without connecting to an endpoint: the client keeps its plugins, serialization and error mapping, and only the transport is replaced. Sharing the client configuration between the production engine and the mock engine - by taking an HttpClientEngine as a constructor parameter - is what makes the test exercise the real client rather than a parallel construction.
pitfalls: MockEngine returns raw bytes, so it does not validate the serialized shape the way the real service would: a wrong content type or a missing field passes silently.
Test and production engines must share one client configuration, otherwise the test proves behaviour of a client that does not ship.
